title: As far as I’m concerned
details:
Example: As far as I’m concerned, we should stay.

Usage: Neutral; introduce a firm personal opinion.

title: I’m in two minds
details:
Example: I’m in two minds about moving.

Usage: Informal; follow with about and a noun or -ing form.

title: I have mixed feelings
description: I feel both positive and negative.
details:
Example: I have mixed feelings about the news.

Usage: Neutral; express conflicting emotions.

title: I’m not convinced
details:
Example: I’m not convinced this will work.

Usage: Neutral; disagree without sounding absolute.

title: I couldn’t agree more
details:
Example: I couldn’t agree more with you.

Usage: Neutral; emphatic agreement.

title: That doesn’t sit right with me
description: That makes me feel morally uncomfortable.
details:
Example: That decision doesn’t sit right with me.

Usage: Conversational; express unease about fairness or ethics.

title: I’m leaning towards
details:
Example: I’m leaning towards the smaller flat.

Usage: Neutral; a preference that is not final.

title: I’m on the fence
description: I have not taken a side.
details:
Example: I’m on the fence about the proposal.

Usage: Informal; remain undecided in a debate.

title: It’s not my cup of tea
description: It does not suit my taste.
details:
Example: Camping isn’t my cup of tea.

Usage: Informal British expression; a gentle dislike.

title: I’m quite keen on
details:
Example: I’m quite keen on that idea.

Usage: Conversational; follow with a noun or -ing form.

title: I’m fed up with
description: I am annoyed by something continuing.
details:
Example: I’m fed up with these delays.

Usage: Informal; stronger than simply bored.

title: I’m over the moon
details:
Example: I’m over the moon about the offer.

Usage: Informal; celebrate very good news.

title: I’m a bit apprehensive
description: I am slightly anxious about what’s ahead.
details:
Example: I’m a bit apprehensive about tomorrow.

Usage: Neutral; anticipation of something uncertain.

title: It’s a weight off my shoulders
details:
Example: Getting the results is a weight off my shoulders.

Usage: Conversational; relief after uncertainty.

title: I take your point
details:
Example: I take your point, but it costs too much.

Usage: Neutral; acknowledge an argument before responding.

title: I beg to differ
details:
Example: I beg to differ on that point.

Usage: Formal; can sound pointed in casual conversation.

title: I wouldn’t go that far
description: I think that claim is too strong.
details:
Example: It’s good, but I wouldn’t go that far.

Usage: Conversational; moderate an exaggerated opinion.

title: I’m all for it
details:
Example: A longer lunch break? I’m all for it.

Usage: Informal; enthusiastic support.

title: I have my reservations
details:
Example: I have my reservations about the timetable.

Usage: Neutral; cautious criticism.

title: It means a lot to me
details:
Example: Your support means a lot to me.

Usage: Neutral; express sincere appreciation.
